discussion_comments.comment_body: Fixed in aa52079cc. LM Studio groups every downloaded quantization of a Hub model as a variant of one model key (`variants` in `/api/v1/models`). Delete is now only offered, and `delete()` refuses otherwise, when the model has a single variant, so it can't remove a quantization the user didn't pick.

vLLM's `/v1/models` reports the window as `max_model_len` (it's on its ModelCard), so a vLLM source still falls back to 128K even though the comment at the top lists vLLM. Worth adding `entry.max_model_len` here?

On LM Studio's `/api/v0/models`, `max_context_length` is the model's ceiling, and a loaded model also reports `loaded_context_length`, which is what it actually serves (can be a lot smaller). Since maxInputTokens falls back to contextWindow and that's the compaction budget, compaction won't kick in before LM Studio starts rejecting. Prefer `loaded_context_length` when it's present?

Fixed in 595b17fec: the object-likeness early return now applies only below the root. A bare or scalar-only root schema (empty MCP inputSchema included) still comes out as `{ type: "object" }`, matching what Gemini requires for tool parameters. Covered by the new root-default test.

discussion_comments.comment_body: This is not quite true for the bare `openai.gpt-6-astra` case. Registering the model here avoids catalog-dependent model selection, but `createBedrockProviderModule` still calls `resolveBedrockModelId`, which consults the generated Bedrock catalog and rewrites this ID to `us.openai.gpt-6-astra` in `us-east-1`. The explicit `us.*` and `global.*` cases already cover the regression, so this does not block the fix, but please narrow this comment (and the matching PR claim) rather than saying no assertion depends on the catalog.

discussion_comments.comment_body: Correct, and thanks for the precision. Registering the model only takes model *selection* off the catalog; `resolveBedrockModelId` still consults it, and with #14480 on main the bare `openai.gpt-6-astra` case goes out as `us.openai.gpt-6-astra` in us-east-1. The test now captures the request path: the `us.*` and `global.*` cases assert they pass through unchanged (no catalog involved), and the bare case is named for what it checks, that the OpenAI shape comes out whichever profile the resolver picks. Comment and PR description narrowed accordingly.
